name: Town Center and Ram Raja Temple
description: The compact core around the still-active Ram Raja Temple and the bustling bazaar is where daily life, ritual and travel logistics converge. Temple bells, chai stalls, guesthouses and rooftop cafes cluster within easy walking distance, putting you at the center of everything Orchha offers.
bestFor: First-time visitors who want everything within a short stroll
pros: Plenty of guesthouses and rooftop cafes
cons: Can be busy and noisy near the temple

name: Orchha Fort and Jehangir Mahal Side
description: The area around the Orchha Fort complex, home to the Raja Mahal and the towering Jehangir Mahal, offers a quieter, more monumental setting. A short walk from the town center across the old bridge, it trades bustle for grand stonework, sweeping views and a heritage atmosphere at every turn.
bestFor: History lovers and photographers wanting palace views

name: Betwa Riverside and Royal Chhatris
description: Along the Betwa river, the row of royal chhatris (cenotaphs) glows gold at sunset, making this the most magical corner of Orchha. Riverside stays and cafes here offer calm, water views and birdlife, a serene base for slow mornings and unforgettable evenings by the flowing Betwa.
bestFor: Slow travelers chasing peace and sunset views

name: Jhansi
description: About 18km away, Jhansi is the practical gateway to Orchha and the wider region. As a proper city, it offers the main railway station with fast trains to Delhi, Agra and connections toward Khajuraho, plus more hotels, shops and services than the heritage town can provide.
bestFor: Travelers needing transport links and city amenities
pros: Major railhead with fast long-distance trains
Wider choice of hotels and services
